description:
We are a team of 4 who are good at web-design, ML and pitching. 

1 main speaker, 2 people who work on ML/backend and 1 designer

We worked together, winning in past competitions.

We are looking for someone who is ready to spend a large amount of time working hard on this hackathon and has prior experience in hackathons.
summary: Hidden Floods is a simple, single-page website built for NASA Space Apps 2026. It shows floodwater hiding under trees and crops—water that normal camera satellites cannot see. We solve this by using NASA’s NISAR L-band radar, a special signal that passes through tree canopies to map the flooding underneath. The site is static and instant (no complex background servers or setup); it simply reads local files to display an Amber map for hidden floods and a Blue map for open lakes and rivers. Its importance lies in making this free radar mapping possible for five regions (Bangladesh, Amazon, Assam, Mali, Pakistan).
details: Hidden Floods maps flooding hidden under trees and crops. Normal maps see only open water. We use NASA NISAR L-band radar HH/HV GCOV data at 20 metre resolution. Each pixel is compared to its own dry-season baseline from the same track since January 2026. Flooded vegetation brightens by double-bounce, coloured amber. Open water darkens by specular reflection, coloured blue. Thresholds use Otsu on our own histograms, floored at twice robust noise. Patches under 0.05 square kilometres are dropped. Confidence is high, medium, or low by signal strength. Five regions were processed: Bangladesh, Amazon, Assam, Mali, and Pakistan. Between 71 and 99 percent of mapped flooding was hidden. The Leaflet website reads a manifest and shows maps, area numbers, a toggle for what others see, and a ranked list of worst areas to check on the ground. Benefits include a fuller picture for aid teams, officials, farm agencies, and researchers. Impact is free, systematic L-band mapping anyone can reuse. Tools were Python (h5py, NumPy, Pillow, pyproj, earthaccess), JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Leaflet, on a Windows laptop. Creativity is the one-click comparison and size-times-confidence ranking. Factors include one season only, 12-day gaps, unreliable towns, wet rice paddies, and provisional, not validated status overall.
